# The Multisensory Networks of Iconic Language

Load packages
```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,   # hide warnings
  message = FALSE,   # hide messages 
  error = FALSE      # hide errors
)
#list of packages (Diveica et al., 2025)
packages <- c("tidyverse", "bootnet", "NetworkComparisonTest", "qgraph", "igraph", "papaja", "ggcorrplot", "rstatix", "psych", "ggrepel", "ggExtra")

#load each package
for (pkg in packages) {
  library(pkg, character.only = TRUE, quietly=TRUE)
}

# notin operator (Diveica et al, 2025)
'%notin%' <- negate('%in%')
```

R environment, version info for reproducibility 
```{r session-info, include=TRUE}
sessionInfo() 
```

Load datasets 
``` {r datasets}
setwd('/Users/ailani/Projects/iconic-network-analysis/data/')

AOA <- read_csv('kuperman_2012_AOA.csv')
lanc <- read_csv('Lancaster_sensorimotor_norms_for_39707_words.csv')
emot <- read_csv('warriner_2013_affective_norms.csv')
icon <- read_csv("winter_2024_iconicity_ratings_cleaned.csv")
```

Select relevant columns from each dataset
```{r}
AOA <- AOA %>% select(Word, Rating.Mean) %>% 
  rename(AOA = Rating.Mean)

lanc <- lanc %>% select(Word, Auditory.mean:Torso.mean) %>% 
  mutate(Word = tolower(Word)) %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "\\.mean"), Auditory.mean:Torso.mean)

emot <- emot %>% select(Word, A.Mean.Sum, V.Mean.Sum) %>% 
  mutate(Valence_Extremity = abs(V.Mean.Sum - 5)) %>% # Get the valence extremity value
  mutate(Valence = V.Mean.Sum) %>%  # Including normal valence scores as well
  rename(Arousal = A.Mean.Sum) %>% 
  select(Word, Arousal, Valence, Valence_Extremity)

icon <- icon %>% select(word, rating, rating_sd)  %>% #make sure if rating is right column 
  rename(Word = word, Iconicity = rating, Iconicity_SD = rating_sd) 
```
I included both Valence and Valence Extremeity. 


Join each dimension ratings to full dataset 
```{r}
df <- reduce(list(AOA, lanc, emot, icon), inner_join, by = "Word")
```

See how many words overlapped
```{r}
nrow(df)
```

There are `r nrow(df)` overlapping words across all the data sets representing the properties of interest.  

### Creating Iconic and Non-iconic Word Groups 
Split into two data frames: one with high iconicity words (`high_iconic`) and another with low iconicity - more arbitrary - words (`low_iconic`). For lack of conventions in iconicity literature, use tertile split. I will also filter to include only iconic rating SDs that are equal to or lower than 1.5, following De Zubicaray & Hinojosa (2026), to make sure iconic ratings have reasonable inter-rater agreement (Pollock, 2018). 
```{r}
# Find the tertile cutoffs on iconicity ratings 
tertiles <- quantile(df$Iconicity, probs= c(1/3, 2/3), na.rm=TRUE)
cut_low <- tertiles[1]
cut_high <- tertiles[2]

# Split into high-iconicity and low-iconicity word groups, filtering for lower SD in iconicity ratings
high_iconic <- df %>% filter(Iconicity >= cut_high) %>%
  filter(Iconicity_SD <= 1.5)
low_iconic <- df %>% filter(Iconicity <= cut_low) %>%
  filter(Iconicity_SD <= 1.5)
```

Check size of the two groups:
```{r}
nrow(high_iconic)
nrow(low_iconic)
```

There are fewer `high_iconic` words (_n_ = `{r} nrow(high_iconic)`) than `low_iconic` (_n_ = `{r} nrow(low_iconic)`), so match to `high_iconic`:
```{r}
n_match <- min(nrow(high_iconic), nrow(low_iconic))

high_iconic <- high_iconic %>% 
  arrange(desc(Iconicity)) %>% #descending order
  slice_head(n=n_match) %>%
  mutate(Iconic = "Iconic")

low_iconic <- low_iconic %>% 
  arrange(Iconicity) %>% #ascending order
  slice_head(n=n_match) %>%
  mutate(Iconic = "Non-iconic")
```

Check if the rows of the split data sets are equal, along with their respective means and ranges 
```{r}
# Check  
nrow(high_iconic) == nrow(low_iconic)
mean(high_iconic$Iconicity); range(high_iconic$Iconicity); sd(high_iconic$Iconicity)

mean(low_iconic$Iconicity);  range(low_iconic$Iconicity); 
sd(low_iconic$Iconicity)
```

Also get the mean of the SDs (inter-rater variability) for each group
``` {r}
high_iconic %>% summarise(mean_sd = mean(Iconicity_SD, na.rm=TRUE))
low_iconic %>% summarise(mean_sd = mean(Iconicity_SD, na.rm=TRUE))

df %>% summarise(mean_SD_full = mean(Iconicity_SD, na.rm=TRUE))
```

Now, both high iconic group and low iconic group have same number of words: `{r} nrow(low_iconic)`.

The mean iconicity of the high_iconic set is 5.20, _SD_ = 0.66, and the range is 4.17-6.92. 

The mean iconicity of the low_iconic set is 2.59, _SD_ = 0.41, and the range is 1.30 - 3.25.

Mean inter-rater SD was 1.22 for high_iconic and 1.28 for low_iconic. The full dataset mean SD of 1.82. 

Middle dataset SD for comparison: 
```{r}
# Checking what the SD of the middle of the dataset (middle iconic ratings) looks like
t.test(df$Iconicity_SD, mu = 1.775)  # 1.775 = combined High/Low mean, adjust as needed

middle_icon_words <- df %>% 
  filter(Iconicity > cut_low, Iconicity < cut_high)

mean(middle_icon_words$Iconicity_SD, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Combine the split data sets into one (removing the middle iconicity words)
```{r}
#Remove Iconicity ratings from high_iconic and low_iconic
high_iconic <- high_iconic %>% select(-Iconicity, -Iconicity_SD)
low_iconic <- low_iconic %>% select(-Iconicity, -Iconicity_SD)

data_both <- bind_rows(high_iconic, low_iconic) %>%
  select(Word, Iconic, everything()) %>%
  mutate(Iconic = factor(Iconic, levels = c("Iconic", "Non-iconic")))
```

### Univariate group comparison of semantic dimensions between high iconic vs low iconic words. 
Adjust for multiple comparisons with Bonferroni correction (following Diveica et al., 2025). 
```{r}
# t-tests to compare ratings between high-iconic vs low-iconic 
stat_test <- data_both %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(3:ncol(data_both), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Rating") %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(Measure) %>%
  rstatix::t_test(Rating ~ Iconic) %>%
  rstatix::adjust_pvalue(p.col = "p", method = "bonferroni") %>%
  rstatix::add_significance(p.col = "p.adj") %>%
  dplyr::select(Measure, statistic, p, p.adj, p.adj.signif) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Add effect sizes with Cohen's d 
effect_sizes <- data_both %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(3:ncol(data_both), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Rating") %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(Measure) %>%
  rstatix::cohens_d(Rating ~ Iconic) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(effsize, magnitude) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

```

Combining descriptive statistics with effect sizes into a results table. 
```{r}
descript <- data_both %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(3:ncol(data_both), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Rating")%>%
  dplyr::group_by(Measure, Iconic) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Mean=mean(Rating), SD = sd(Rating), Skew= psych::skew(Rating), Kurtosis = psych::kurtosi(Rating)) %>%
  mutate('Mean Score (SD)' = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", Mean), " (", sprintf("%.2f", SD), ")")) %>%
  select(-Mean, -SD) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Iconic, values_from = c('Mean Score (SD)', Skew, Kurtosis))

#generate results table 
result_table <- dplyr::bind_cols(descript %>% 
  select(Measure, starts_with("Mean")), 
  stat_test %>% dplyr::select(-Measure), effect_sizes) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(effsize))

```

#### Visualize the differences with violin plots
``` {r}
# Build plot of dimension-based ratings for high-iconic and low-iconic words, annotating by effect size 

# Long form of data 
dat <- data_both %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(3:ncol(data_both), names_to = "Measure", values_to= "Rating")
dat <- left_join(dat, result_table %>% 
  dplyr::select(Measure, effsize), by = "Measure") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Measure = factor(Measure, levels=result_table$Measure), 
  Iconic = factor(Iconic, levels = c("Iconic", "Non-iconic")))

# Violin Plot Formatting
fig1 <- ggplot2::ggplot(dat, 
    aes(x = Iconic, y = Rating, split=Iconic, fill= Iconic)) +
    ggplot2::geom_violin(position="identity", alpha=0.5, aes(color = Iconic)) +
    ggplot2::stat_summary(
      fun.data = "mean_cl_normal", fun.args = list(conf.int = .99),
      geom = "errorbar", linewidth = 1,
      width = .2
    ) + 
    ggplot2::geom_text(aes(label = paste0("d = ", format(effsize, digits = 2)), x = 1.5, y = Inf),
      vjust = 1.5, hjust = 0.5, size = 3, color = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "point") +
    ggplot2::stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "line", aes(group = 1), linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(vars(Measure), ncol = 4, scales = "free_y", 
      labeller = labeller(Measure = c("Iconicity_val" = "Iconicity"))) + 
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("#3160d7", "#ed968c")) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c("#3160d7", "#ed968c")) +
    ggplot2::labs(x="", y="Score") + 
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank()) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3))
```

Violin plots of each of the semantic rating distribution for low iconicity and high iconicity words. The formatting reflects the one done in Diveica's 2025 paper: the means and the 99% confidence intervals are illustrated, the dashed lines show the effect direction, and the Cohen's _d_ is written below the semantic dimension name. 

```{r descriptives viz, include = TRUE}
fig1
papaja::apa_table(result_table)
```


Olfactory, Gustatory, Auditory, Mouth dimensions were not significant between high iconicity and low iconicity words. Interoceptive (_p_ = .022, _d_ = .16) and Visual (_p_ = .002, _d_ = 0.20) dimensions had negligible effect sizes. All other dimensions were statistically significant (_p_s < .0003). 

High iconicity words had higher Haptic, Hand/arm, Arousal, Foot/leg, Torso, and Valence Extremity mean ratings than low iconicity words. 

Low iconicity words had higher Head, Valence, and Age of Acquisition mean ratings than high iconicity words. 

### Correlation martix for full data set 
``` {r}
library(dplyr)
cor_data <- df %>%
  select(2:(ncol(df)-1))

cor_matrix <- cor(cor_data, use="pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# get p-values for correlations 
library(Hmisc)

rcorr_result <- rcorr(as.matrix(cor_data), type = "pearson")

#rcorr_result$r  # correlation coefficients
#rcorr_result$P  # p-values

# Visualize
library(corrplot)
corrplot(cor_matrix, 
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         #order = "hclust",
         p.mat = rcorr_result$P,
         sig.level = 0.05,
         insig = "blank",       # blank out non-significant cells
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.6,
         tl.col = "black",
         title = "Full (Iconic and Non-iconic groups combined)",
         tl.srt = 45,
         diag = FALSE)
```


``` {r, include = FALSE} 
# Separate correlation matrices for high vs low iconic groups 
cor_hi_data <- high_iconic %>%
  select(2:(ncol(df)-2))
cor_low_data <- low_iconic %>%
  select(2:(ncol(df)-2))

cor_high <- cor(cor_hi_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cor_low  <- cor(cor_low_data,  use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

corrplot(cor_high, method = "color", type = "upper", addCoef.col = "black", 
         number.cex = 0.5, tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45, diag = FALSE,
         title = "High iconicity", mar = c(0,0,2,0))

corrplot(cor_low, method = "color", type = "upper", addCoef.col = "black", 
         number.cex = 0.5, tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45, diag = FALSE,
         title = "Low iconicity", mar = c(0,0,2,0))
```

# Independent Networks 

## Estimate the partial correlation networks. 

Select rows that will be used as nodes (remove `Word`, `Iconic` columns) from `high_iconic` and `low_iconic` data frames. 
```{r prepare data}
nrow(high_iconic) == nrow(low_iconic)

high_iconic <- high_iconic %>% 
  select(-Word, -Iconic)

low_iconic <- low_iconic %>% 
  select(-Word, -Iconic)

# variable to store label names of nodes
names <- as.list(names(low_iconic))
```

Estimate network for each group, using `bootnet` package. 
```{r partial correlation networks}
#| output: false
net_high <- estimateNetwork(high_iconic,
  default = "EBICglasso", 
  corMethod = "cor_auto",
  tuning = 0.5)

net_low <- estimateNetwork(low_iconic,
  default = "EBICglasso", 
  corMethod = "cor_auto",
  tuning = 0.5)

L <- averageLayout(net_low,net_high)
```

```{r side-by-side networks, include=TRUE}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Plot the networks for both groups
plot(net_low, layout="circle",label.scale = FALSE, title = "Low Iconicity Network")
plot(net_high, layout = "circle",label.scale = FALSE, title = "High Iconicity Network")
```



Create partial correlation plots
```{r partial correlation matrices}
#| output: false
pcor_high <- net_high$graph
pcor_low <- net_low$graph

# add column and row names 
colnames(pcor_high) <- rownames(pcor_high) <- colnames(high_iconic)
colnames(pcor_low)  <- rownames(pcor_low)  <- colnames(low_iconic)

matrix1 <- corrplot::corrplot(
  pcor_high,
  method = "color",
  type="upper",
  addCoef.col = "black", 
  tl.col = "black", 
  number.cex = 0.5, 
  tl.srt = 45, 
  diag = FALSE,
  mar = c(0,0,2,0),
  title = "High Iconicity: Partial Correlations"
)

matrix2 <- corrplot::corrplot(
  pcor_low,
  method = "color",
  type="upper",
  addCoef.col = "black", 
  tl.col = "black", 
  number.cex = 0.5, 
  tl.srt = 45, 
  diag = FALSE,
  mar = c(0,0,2,0),
  title = "Low Iconicity: Partial Correlations"
)
```

### Combined Partial Correlation Plots
Upper triangle is the partial correlations of high_iconic group, while the lower triangle is the pcorrs of the low_iconic group. 
```{r combined pcorr plot, include = TRUE}
# Combine the partial correlation plots into one [COME BACK LATER]
combined_matrix <- pcor_high # Use high_iconic as base 
combined_matrix[upper.tri(combined_matrix)] <- pcor_low[upper.tri(pcor_low)] #fill upper with low_iconic corrplot 

pc_corrplot <- ggcorrplot(
  combined_matrix, # combined partial correlation plot
  type = "full",
  legend.title = "Partial r", 
  show.diag = TRUE,
  outline.col = "white",
  lab = TRUE, # display correlation coef 
  lab_size = 2, 
  tl.cex = 8, # size of text labels on axes
  tl.col = "black", 
  hc.order = FALSE
)
pc_corrplot
```

## Centrality metrics 
Create centrality figure 
```{r centrality plot, include = TRUE}
centralityPlot(list(High = net_high, Low = net_low), include = c("Strength"), decreasing = FALSE, orderBy = "Strength", scale="raw", theme_bw = TRUE)

```

Centrality Table
```{r centrality table, include = FALSE}
centrality_table_raw <- centralityTable(net_high, net_low, standardized = FALSE)
centrality_table_z <- centralityTable(net_high, net_low, standardized = TRUE)

centrality_table_z %>% 
  filter(measure == "Strength") %>% 
  arrange(desc(value))
```
